notes: Clean reference-like fix but omits the quoted-address suffix guard; thorough segment-level tests including backticks and heredoc.
Clean Token-method helpers applied consistently with good segment-level tests, but it misses the quoted-token exemption on the 'address ends with {' check.
Full coverage of all brace checks via bounds-safe Dispenser helpers (slightly over-abstracted with isStructural), with good dispenser, parse, and adapter tests.

Covers every structural brace site the reference changes, including the quoted HasSuffix address check and the quoted '{}' handling, though the isStructural helper with its own bounds check is slightly over-engineered.

Core fix is right, but it exports new Token API, skips the quoted-address suffix check, keeps the old quoted '{}' branch, reorders doImport needlessly, and adds lexer tests for behavior it did not change.

Core fix is correct, but it adds exported Token API, leaves the 'address ends with {' check firing on quoted tokens, and keeps the old quoted-'{}' branch; the added lexer tests don't exercise the change and are partly duplicated.
Matches the reference functionally, but adds redundant Dispenser-level wrappers on top of the Token helpers; tests are broad, including an import/snippet case and an integration adapt file.
Complete fix covering all reference sites, with thorough dispenser, parser, snippet and integration tests, though the duplicated Dispenser wrappers over the Token helpers add needless indirection.
Matches the reference: unexported Token helpers cover every structural brace check, including the address suffix and the quoted '{}' handling, and the dispenser and parser tests are focused.
Faithful, consistent equivalent of the reference using unexported Token helpers, with focused dispenser and parser tests including backtick quoting.
Correct core fix with clean helpers, but leaves quoted '{}' entering the special branch, unlike the reference; adds a reasonable integration adapt test.
Correct and consistent helpers, but it keeps the original quoted-'{}' branch structure, so quoted '{}' still skips the new-line break check; adds a reasonable adapt integration test.
Essentially the reference fix with clean Token helpers, including the address suffix and quoted '{}' handling; dispenser and parse tests cover nested and same-line cases well.
Essentially matches the reference including the HasSuffix and '{}' fixes, with a minor inconsistency in doImport where it uses an inline check instead of the helper.
Complete fix using Dispenser helpers, though it mixes inline Quoted() checks with the helpers; nice test for a quoted '{' as a site address.
Complete and correct, matching the reference site-for-site, but it mixes dispenser helpers with inline `== "{" && !Quoted()` checks and re-indents the doImport switch under an outer if.

Over-engineered collector that exports a configs helper and still overrides per resource across modules; it also silently drops a static block when mixed with a for_each import block for the same resource in one module, which is a new variant of the bug.

Its collector still dedups across modules by ConfigResource, and within one module it drops a static block when a for_each block targets the same resource (and the reverse), so it creates new silent drops; it also exports a configs helper the fix did not need.

Instance-aware ancestor override via static parsing handles the common parent/child case, but falls back to whole-resource override for dynamic targets and module-instance keys, reimplements key comparison, and edits CHANGELOG.md directly; tests are thorough.

Instance-level parent/child override via static parsing fixes the reported case and the static cross-module case, but re-implements address parsing and still drops child blocks when either side uses for_each or keyed module instances, which expansion-time dedup would handle.
Same per-resource cross-module override as C2 (child blocks for other instances get discarded), with a nice aliasing fix and solid unit plus ordering-variant plan tests.
Same ConfigResource-level cross-module dedup as C4 (so the instance-level override case is missed), with a nice slice-aliasing fix and order-permutation and unit tests.

Fixes same-module for_each/count imports, but still deduplicates across modules per ConfigResource, so a parent block for one instance silently drops child blocks for other instances; good unit, plan and apply tests.
Correct for same-module for_each/count, with good plan, apply and unit tests, but ConfigResource-level parent override still silently discards child imports for other instances.
Keeps all same-module blocks but overrides at resource rather than instance level across modules, missing the parent/child different-instance case; only a single basic plan test.
Allows same-module duplicates via a claiming-module map, but still drops child-module blocks for other instances whenever a parent targets the same resource.

Same approach as the reference: it returns every import statement and deduplicates per resource instance inside expandResourceImports, so parent blocks override child blocks per instance; the modCtx refactor and module-path aliasing fix are defensible extras, but it adds only one same-module for_each test.

Matches the reference: it returns all statements and dedups per instance at expansion time (first, i.e. parent, wins), and also fixes the cfg.Path append aliasing; the modCtx refactor is minor extra churn and the tests cover only the basic for_each case.

Set-based per-module claiming fixes the reported case but still discards child-module blocks whenever an ancestor touches the same resource; somewhat convoluted pointer/claiming bookkeeping and a minimal test.
Fixes the single-module case cleanly, but parent/child override is still per ConfigResource, so a parent import for one instance silently discards child blocks for other instances.
Same per-resource cross-module dedup as C2-C5, so child imports of other instances are lost when a parent imports one instance; its single plan test only covers the root-module for_each case.
Fixes the single-module case, but cross-module override still drops child blocks for other instances; the redundant TargetContains check and the 'undefined order' doc are slightly confusing.
